native_result.query: What proportion of original studies in Experimental Economics were conducted in the United Kingdom?
native_result.HypoA: The original studies in Experimental Economics were primarily conducted in the United States (61.1%), while the replication studies were more distributed across countries like Austria (27.8%), Germany (11.1%), Singapore (27.8%), the United Kingdom (11.1%), and the United States (22.2%).
native_result.HypoB: Among the original studies of the Experimental Economics replication project (project == 'ee') in this dataset, 1 of 18 (5.56%, 95% Wilson CI 0.99%-25.76%) were conducted in the United Kingdom: the single case is Huck, Seltzer and Wallace (AER 2011), id ee.13, n = 120, which was not replicated. The same proportion holds whether or not rows with a missing original country are excluded (1/18 = 5.56%), because no ee row has a missing country. The field is dominated by the United States (11/18 = 61.11%), followed by Germany and Switzerland (2 each) and by Australia and Austria (1 each), so being conducted in the UK was rare in this sample -- and it is not implied by language, since 13/18 originals used English yet only one was in the UK. Scope limit: these files contain only the 18 originals of the Experimental Economics project available here (16 in the American Economic Review, 2 in the Quarterly Journal of Economics), one row per original study with a single replication each. Any additional originals that a broader published catalogue of this replication project may contain are simply absent from these files, so this proportion is a property of these 18 sampled originals and is not an estimate of the full catalogue, about which these data support no claim.
native_result.WorkflowB: 1) Loaded meta-regression_study_data (927x57); filtered project=='ee' -> 18 rows, one per original study (unique ids ee.1-ee.18, titles, authors; 0 duplicates, 0 drop==True, 0 aggregated, 0 multi-lab). 2) Normalised experiment_country.o (lowercase, whitespace collapse, trailing dot) and applied the STRICT UK criterion against {united kingdom, uk, u.k, great britain, britain, england, scotland, wales}; only 'United Kingdom' matched. 3) Computed numerator (1) over both denominators: all ee rows (18) and rows with non-missing country (18) -- identical because ee has zero missing countries. 4) Computed the 95% Wilson interval by hand and verified it independently plus with statsmodels (Wilson 0.99-25.76; Clopper-Pearson 0.14-27.29 as a wider reference). 5) Built context tables (country, original language, journal x year) and the audit trail of all 18 originals. 6) The second CSV was NOT used in the computation because it has no country column (verified programmatically); its only role was the 1:1 validation of the 18 EERP originals by first-author surname (now EXACT 18/18 after fixing string-cleaning artefacts).
